title: Jonah and the Plant
reflectionText: A vine came up in a night and perished in a night, and Jonah cared more for its shade than for a city of a hundred twenty thousand. Twice God asked whether his anger was right. The book ends before Jonah answers. Have you ever been left holding God's question about Nineveh, and all those people who cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-08-01, Batch I. Owner-approved anchor Jonah 4, whole chapter, no verses excluded. Written as the CODA to 1100 (Jonah 3, Nineveh repents), not as a middle beat; the repentance of Nineveh is not re-told. Both lanes originally opened with the clause 'The city was spared', which reports Jonah 3:10 and therefore fell outside the registered Jonah 4 anchor; that clause was an out-of-anchor event, not neutral connective narration. A source-boundary repair removed it from both lanes on 2026-08-06 and re-anchored Jonah as the subject of the first sentence in each. Both lanes now begin inside Jonah 4:1, and Jonah's own prayer in 4:2 supplies the reason for his anger, as the chapter itself does. Ends on God's question, unanswered, as the chapter does. WEB 'vine' and 'Yahweh'; KJV 'gourd' and 'the Lord'. Journey backlog item G16. TEXT APPROVED — AUDIO AUTHORIZED BY OWNER ON 2026-08-01.
